title: An agent loop is bounded by an iteration count, not by cumulative spend, so the cap holds while the bill does not
problem: I set the turn limit the docs told me to set, and I still woke up to a four-figure bill, because nothing in my loop ever knew how much money it had left.
symptom: The run stays inside its configured turn or step limit and raises nothing, so no alert fires; the overspend is discovered on the invoice or the provider usage dashboard, hours or days after the money is gone.
why_now: Every mainstream agent runtime ships a turn or step counter as its only terminating bound and none ships a cumulative token or dollar ceiling that halts a run in flight. Per-turn context has grown by orders of magnitude as tool definitions and history are re-sent every turn, so a fixed iteration count no longer bounds cost at all: the same 50-turn cap can mean cents or hundreds of dollars depending on how wide the context got.
existing: OpenAI Agents SDK max_turns: bounds turns only, says nothing about tokens or money, and is explicitly disable-able by passing None.
LangGraph recursion_limit: a step counter whose documented remedy for hitting it is to pass a higher limit.
Per-request max_tokens: bounds one completion, never the sum over a run.
Provider spend dashboards and monthly budget alerts: detective rather than preventive, evaluated on aggregates after the calls have been billed, and unable to terminate an in-flight run.

evidence.title: [BUG]  Claude Code sends repeated requests hundreds of times without stopping
evidence.quote: Add a maximum retry limit or cumulative cost guardrail for unattended sessions.
evidence.note: The reporter names the missing primitive in his own words after an unattended session cost him over 500 dollars. He is asking the vendor for a cumulative spend ceiling, which is exactly the primitive that does not exist.

evidence.title: Running agents - OpenAI Agents SDK
evidence.quote: If we exceed the max_turns passed, we raise a MaxTurnsExceeded exception. Pass max_turns=None to disable this turn limit.
evidence.note: The only run-terminating bound the SDK documents is a turn count, and it can be switched off entirely. Page carries no publication date, so the date field is the date I fetched it.

evidence.title: GRAPH_RECURSION_LIMIT - Docs by LangChain
evidence.quote: Your LangGraph StateGraph reached the maximum number of steps before hitting a stop condition.
evidence.note: The framework's runaway-loop guard is a step counter, and the documented remedy for hitting it is to raise the counter. Page carries no publication date, so the date field is the date I fetched it.

build_hypothesis: A budget object threaded through the run: a cumulative token and dollar counter incremented from every response usage field, checked immediately before each model call, raising a typed BudgetExhausted that returns the partial result rather than discarding it - plus a non-None default read from the environment, so an unattended run is never accidentally unbounded.

check.manual_question: Your agent loop declares an iteration cap. Is there also a cumulative token or dollar ceiling, accumulated from response usage and checked before each model call, that terminates the run in flight? If the only answer is a provider dashboard or a monthly budget alert, the run is unbounded.
check.rationale: A repository that names an iteration bound has thought about termination, which makes the absence of any cumulative-spend identifier meaningful rather than incidental. What it can get wrong: a project may enforce spend in a gateway, proxy or sidecar outside this repository, in which case the verdict is a false positive - and a project that merely mentions a budget name without checking it before the call reads as mitigated when it is not, which is why both signatures matching escalates to MANUAL.

bad.agent/loop.py:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI()
MAX_TURNS = 50  # the only bound this loop has


def run(task, max_turns=MAX_TURNS):
    messages = [{"role": "user", "content": task}]
    for _turn in range(max_turns):
        reply = client.chat.completions.create(model="gpt-5", messages=messages)
        text = reply.choices[0].message.content
        messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": text})
        if "DONE" in text:
            return messages
    raise RuntimeError("turn limit reached")

good.agent/loop.py:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI()
MAX_TURNS = 50
MAX_COST_USD = 2.00


class BudgetExhausted(RuntimeError):
    pass


def run(task, max_turns=MAX_TURNS, max_cost_usd=MAX_COST_USD):
    messages = [{"role": "user", "content": task}]
    cumulative_cost = 0.0
    for _turn in range(max_turns):
        if cumulative_cost >= max_cost_usd:
            raise BudgetExhausted(f"stopped at {cumulative_cost} of {max_cost_usd}")
        reply = client.chat.completions.create(model="gpt-5", messages=messages)
        cumulative_cost += price(reply.usage)
        text = reply.choices[0].message.content
        messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": text})
        if "DONE" in text:
            return messages
    raise RuntimeError("turn limit reached")
